title: The Concept of Quantum Entanglement
text:
Quantum entanglement describes a phenomenon where two or more particles become linked in such a way that the quantum state of each particle cannot be described independently of the others. Measuring the property (such as spin) of one entangled particle instantaneously determines the corresponding property of the other, regardless of the spatial distance separating them.

Einstein famously called this 'spooky action at a distance' because it appears to violate classical notions of locality and realism. While entanglement does not permit faster-than-light communication—as no information can be transmitted purely through correlation—it is a critical resource in emerging fields like quantum computing and quantum cryptography, laying the theoretical groundwork for secure data transfer.
